PeriodsAndSpecialValues.summary: The libraries have none of the motivic infrastructure this roadmap is built on: no motive, no Betti or algebraic de Rham realization, no period torsor, no K-theory beyond K_0, no determinant-line/fundamental-line formalism, no Fitting ideals, no Tamagawa number, no Sha and no multiple zeta values in Mathlib or Tau Ceti. What exists sits one level below the roadmap. Tau Ceti has a sorry-free theory of pure and mixed Hodge structures (opposed filtrations, Hodge pieces, conjugation, Tate twists, polarizations, Deligne splitting, period-domain points), the top exterior power with endomorphisms acting by det, and Tannakian reconstruction for Hopf algebras. Mathlib has the analytic special-value theory: Dirichlet L-functions with continuation, Gamma factors, completed L-functions, root numbers and functional equations; Riemann and Hurwitz zeta at negative integers via Bernoulli numbers and polynomials; zeta(2k); the Dedekind zeta function with the Dirichlet class number formula; the unit regulator; the completed L-function of a modular form with entire continuation for cusp forms; and the Gauss hypergeometric function. Even the starting points of PS.0 and PS.1 are incomplete: there is no real Frobenius F_infinity or eigenspaces H_B^+-, no generalized Bernoulli numbers or rationality of Dirichlet L-values, and no periods of modular forms. Periods as objects, formal periods, motivic cohomology and Beilinson regulators, integral fundamental lines, ETNC, BSD/Bloch-Kato assembly, certified enclosures, Picard-Fuchs/mirror symmetry and MZVs are all absent, so no layer is even partly built.

targets.target: Betti/de Rham realization comparison matrices for a motive with a chosen complex embedding
targets.note: Neither library has motives, algebraic de Rham cohomology of a variety, or a Betti realization. Mathlib has Kaehler differentials (KaehlerDifferential, 127 declarations) but no de Rham complex of a scheme; the only 'DeRham' names in Mathlib are the perfectoid period rings BDeRham/BDeRhamPlus in Mathlib/RingTheory/Perfectoid/BDeRham.lean, which are Fontaine's rings, not a realization functor. Tau Ceti has singular homology (TopPair.singularHomology) and quasi-coherent scheme cohomology, but no comparison between them.

targets.target: Basis-independent determinant lines and the effect of changing bases
targets.note: The linear algebra of a single top exterior power is present: Tau Ceti identifies the top exterior power of a module with a basis indexed by Fin n with the scalars (exteriorPower.topEquiv) and proves an endomorphism acts on it by its determinant (map_top_eq_det_smul, with a basis-free form), which is the change-of-basis rule for the line. Missing is any determinant line/determinant functor formalism (graded lines, Knudsen-Mumford, determinants of complexes) and any statement that a period class is well defined modulo a change of basis.

targets.target: Complex conjugation eigenspaces, Hodge filtration and Tate twists
targets.note: Tau Ceti has the Hodge-theoretic linear algebra, sorry-free: a bounded decreasing filtration opposed to its conjugate in weight n (for any conjugate-linear involution, in particular the one induced by an integral lattice), the Hodge pieces with conjugation exchanging H^{p,q} and H^{q,p}, Tate twists with their effect on F, Hodge numbers, polarizations, rational substructures, mixed Hodge structures and the Deligne splitting. Missing is the 'complex conjugation' of Deligne's period formalism: no real Frobenius F_infinity acting on a Betti realization and hence no eigenspaces H_B^+ and H_B^- (the Conjugation structure is the antilinear involution defining the real form, not F_infinity), and no Hodge structure is produced from a variety.

targets.target: Period classes modulo coefficient-field units; effect of changing embeddings
targets.note: No declaration in either library names a period of a motive or of a variety; grep for 'period' in the name column returns only periodic functions, period lattices of elliptic curves and Tau Ceti's Hodge period domain (TauCeti.Hodge.PeriodDomain.Point), which is the classifying space, not a period matrix.

duplicates.note: MC.2 constructs the realization functors themselves and compares Betti/de Rham realizations over embeddings into C; PS.0 consumes them and is declared to have MC.2 as an input, so the realization-comparison target is stated twice.

C5 owns the algebraic de Rham-Betti comparison for smooth complex varieties, including integral Betti lattices and rational structures retained before complexification; PS.0's comparison matrices are the matrix form of exactly that comparison.

HodgeStructures L0 owns pure Hodge structures with the conjugation symmetry of the Hodge pieces and the Tate twist - the filtration/conjugation/Tate-twist part of PS.0 T2 that TauCeti/Geometry/Hodge now delivers.

targets.target: Completed motivic L-function from local Weil-Deligne data
targets.note: No Weil-Deligne representation and no motivic L-function in either library; grep for weilDeligne/WeilDeligne in names returns nothing, and grep -rn -i 'Weil-Deligne' over both trees returns no definition. The only Euler-product-from-local-data constructions are Tau Ceti's EulerProductData (abstract multiplicative ideal weights) and Mathlib's WeierstrassCurve.LFunction.

targets.target: Critical integers derived from archimedean Gamma factors
targets.note: Mathlib has the archimedean Gamma factor of a Dirichlet character (even and odd cases) and the poles of Gamma, which is what a criticality condition is read off from, but there is no definition of a critical integer and no statement that criticality is a simultaneous regularity condition for two infinity factors.

targets.target: Deligne-type normalized-value statement (sign, powers of 2 pi i, coefficient field, Galois equivariance)
targets.note: Nothing in either library states an algebraicity-up-to-a-period result. There is no period to divide by, and no Galois equivariance statement for L-values.

targets.target: The Dirichlet/Tate case: special values of Dirichlet L-functions with their functional equation and rationality
targets.note: The analytic half is in Mathlib and sorry-free: continuation of L-functions of functions on ZMod N, the completed L-function, the functional equation for primitive characters with explicit root number, zeta(-n) = -B_{n+1}/(n+1), zeta(2k) as a rational multiple of pi^{2k}, and Hurwitz zeta at negative integers via Bernoulli polynomials. The rationality half is missing for nontrivial characters: Mathlib records only the trivial zeros of Dirichlet L-functions, defines no generalized Bernoulli numbers B_{k,chi}, and never states L(chi, 1-k) = -B_{k,chi}/k or its algebraicity (its HurwitzZetaValues TODO asks to extend the values to Dirichlet L-functions). Nothing is phrased as a critical value normalized by a period.

targets.target: The modular-form case with ramified and imprimitive corrections
targets.note: Mathlib defines the completed L-function Lambda and the L-function L of a modular form for an arithmetic subgroup, proves the Dirichlet-series identity on the convergence half-plane and, for cusp forms, entire continuation; its WeakFEPair pairs f with f|S, so the abstract functional equation relates Lambda(f) to Lambda(f|S) (no Fricke/Atkin-Lehner sign for Gamma_0(N)). Tau Ceti adds Hecke's abscissa bounds, identifies the LSeries of the q-expansion coefficients with Mathlib's L, and has Atkin-Lehner and Fricke eigenspace decompositions. There is no period of a modular form, no algebraicity of L(f,j)/period and no treatment of imprimitive or ramified corrections.

duplicates.note: AL.1 (Tate's thesis) defines L, epsilon and the real/complex gamma factors of Hecke characters and proves the global functional equation - the GL_1 archimedean factors of PS.1 T1 and the Dirichlet/Tate case of T3.
AN.1 owns the Dirichlet-series/continuation apparatus PS.1 needs for the Dirichlet/Tate case.
M.8 also exports Galois realisations with their Frobenius Euler polynomials, overlapping PS.1's local-factor bookkeeping.

AL.5 supplies imprimitive/primitive comparisons, critical-value normalization, functional-equation signs and algebraicity inputs for GL_2/Rankin families - PS.1's modular-form case with its imprimitive corrections (T2, T4).
DirichletPadicLFunctions L0 constructs generalized Bernoulli numbers and proves the algebraicity of Dirichlet L-values against the complex L-functions - the missing half of PS.1 T3.
ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions L1 defines period lines Omega_f^+- and proves algebraicity of the period-normalized critical values L(f,chi,j+1) - PS.1's modular-form case (T4).

targets.target: Algebra of formal periods with linearity, change-of-variables and Stokes relations
targets.note: No formal period algebra in either library. Mathlib has the divergence theorem and integration by parts for interval integrals, but nothing that presents an algebra by generators (X, D, omega, gamma) modulo the period relations.

targets.target: Comparison with the coordinate ring of the Nori period torsor
targets.note: No Nori motives, no Tannakian category of motives and no torsor of tensor isomorphisms between two fibre functors. The neutral reconstruction exists: Mathlib proves Tannaka duality for finite groups (TannakaDuality.FiniteGroup.equiv), and Tau Ceti identifies the A-points of a commutative Hopf algebra with tensor automorphisms of the scalar-extension fibre functor on finite-dimensional comodules (TauCeti.Tannaka.fgPointTensorIsoEquiv). A name search for 'Nori' matches only knot-theory names containing 'unoriented'.

targets.target: Evaluation map into C and the separation of forced identities from injectivity
targets.note: Absent for the same reason; there is no period object to evaluate.

duplicates.note: MC.6 constructs tensor-isomorphism torsors between fiber functors and explicitly says it exports period torsors to PeriodsAndSpecialValues; the torsor half of PS.2 is MC.6's target restated.

targets.target: Rational motivic cohomology
targets.note: No motivic cohomology, no higher Chow groups and no higher algebraic K-theory in either library. The only K-theory is Tau Ceti's K_0: Grothendieck groups of split, exact, abelian and triangulated categories, and K_0 of finitely generated projective modules over a ring with the Cartan map; Mathlib's AlgebraicCycle has no rational equivalence or cycle classes.

targets.target: Real/Deligne regulators and leading-term lines
targets.note: No Borel regulator, no Deligne regulator, no Beilinson regulator: the only declarations whose names contain 'regulator' are the Dirichlet unit regulator (Mathlib) and the Neron-Tate regulator of a Weierstrass curve (Tau Ceti).

targets.target: The zero-rank and nonzero-rank Borel cases for a number field, with embedding multiplicities and covolume normalization
targets.note: The weight-one Borel case is the Dirichlet regulator, and that is complete and sorry-free: Mathlib defines the regulator as the determinant of the logarithmic embedding of a fundamental system, proves it positive, independent of the family up to index (regOfFamily_div_regulator), and proves the Dirichlet class number formula as the residue of the Dedekind zeta function at s = 1, with the explicit 2^{r1}(2 pi)^{r2} R h / (w sqrt|d|) constant. Tau Ceti adds the rank-zero degeneration regulator = 1. Higher-weight Borel regulators (K_{2n-1} of a number field to R) are absent, and Mathlib's residue statement is a one-sided real limit, not an analytic continuation of zeta_K.

targets.target: Comparison of higher K-theory and motivic regulators via the actual comparison maps; torsion kept separate from lattices
targets.note: No higher K-theory in either library, so no comparison map exists.

duplicates.note: R.7 owns the Borel/Beilinson comparison, the factor-of-2 normalization and the zero-rank and rank-one recoveries; PS.3's acceptance test restates R.7's.

M.8 constructs the rational regulator from motivic cohomology, the Chern-character compatibility and the separation of integral lattices from rational 'integral parts' - the same three targets as PS.3.
ER.5 owns the elliptic-curve regulator/leading-term example PS.3 lists as an input and re-exports.

targets.target: Integral determinant lines of perfect global/local cohomology complexes
targets.note: Neither library has perfect complexes over a ring or a determinant functor on them; 'IsPerfect' in both trees means a perfect matching or a perfect group, and there is no detLine/determinantFunctor anywhere.

targets.target: Finite/singular local conditions and archimedean corrections, with the real comparison trivialization
targets.note: No Selmer-style local conditions attached to a determinant line; Tau Ceti's continuous cohomology (TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Homological/ContCohomology) provides the cohomology but no finite/singular decomposition.

targets.target: Invariance under quasi-isomorphism and change of lattice
targets.note: Meaningless without the determinant line; no such invariance statement exists.

targets.target: Contribution of finite kernels and cokernels; Fitting ideals versus determinant generators
targets.note: Only the order bookkeeping exists: Mathlib's multiplicativity of cardinalities along a submodule and quotient, and Tau Ceti's Euler-Poincare theorem for any invariant additive on short exact sequences. Neither library defines Fitting ideals of a module - every 'Fitting' declaration is the Fitting decomposition of a Lie module or of an endomorphism (Mathlib Lie/Weights, Tau Ceti KrullSchmidt) - or determinant lines, so the Fitting-versus-determinant comparison the layer insists on cannot be stated.

targets.target: Bad-prime Euler and Tamagawa factors
targets.note: Mathlib defines the local Euler factor of a Weierstrass curve over a nonarchimedean local field, split by good/split multiplicative/nonsplit multiplicative/additive reduction, so the bad-prime Euler factors exist for elliptic curves. No Tamagawa number exists in either library (name search for 'tamagawa' returns nothing).

duplicates.note: D7 owns the compact-support and local-condition cochain complexes of number fields with derived local/global duality and their perfectness and amplitude, with modified real-place terms at p = 2 - the perfect global/local complexes of PS.4 T0 and T1.
M.8 also builds Selmer complexes from explicit local conditions and their determinants for the Tate and elliptic representations.
L2 owns Selmer structures with finite/singular local conditions and their duals, which PS.4 restates as 'finite/singular conditions'.

PMIA L5 constructs determinant lines of perfect complexes compatible with quasi-isomorphism and relates them to characteristic divisors of torsion cohomology and finite modules - PS.4 T0, T2 and T3 (AUDIT-26 lists the reverse link).

L3 asks for the determinant-line formulation of perfect Iwasawa complexes and its relation to characteristic ideals, the Iwasawa-theoretic case of PS.4 T0/T2 (the reverse of the existing L3 -> PS.4 link).

targets.target: Zeta elements and the equivariant Tamagawa-number conjecture in a relative K-group
targets.note: There is no K_1, no relative K-group and no zeta element in either library; Tau Ceti's K-theory stops at K_0 (of exact categories and of finitely generated projective modules).

targets.target: Reduced norms and noncommutative K1 (not replaced by scalar units)
targets.note: No reduced norm of a general central simple or semisimple algebra and no K_1 in either library. The only reduced norm is Tau Ceti's norm form of a quaternion algebra (QuaternionAlgebra.normForm); Mathlib's BrauerGroup is a bare quotient, with the group structure and Br(R) = Z/2 in Tau Ceti.

targets.target: Adapters for the proven Tate/Artin and abelian cases
targets.note: Absent; there is no Artin L-function in either library either (the only L-functions are Dirichlet, modular and Weierstrass).

targets.target: Recovering the commutative determinant formula on specialization
targets.note: Absent for the same reason.

duplicates.note: NE.3 owns reduced norms, SK1 and Artin evaluation, exactly the K1 targets PS.5 restates.
I.7 states the equivariant Tamagawa-number formulation for the integral Brumer-Stark setting, overlapping PS.5's equivariant statements.
NE.5 formulates localized-K1 zeta elements and proves agreement with the commutative determinant formulas on specialization - PS.5 T0 and T3 (AUDIT-26 lists the reverse link).

targets.target: Adapters identifying fundamental-line terms with Mordell-Weil regulator, torsion, local Tamagawa numbers, periods and Sha
targets.note: Of the five terms only the Mordell-Weil regulator and the torsion subgroup exist: Tau Ceti defines the regulator as the absolute determinant of the Neron-Tate Gram matrix with basis-independence and nonnegativity, and proves E(K)_tors finite (finite_torsion) with Nagell-Lutz over Q. Tamagawa numbers, the real period and Sha do not exist in either library, and no adapter to a fundamental line can be formed.

targets.target: Connection to the rank-zero/one BSD owner and scoped Euler-system deductions
targets.note: No Euler system and no BSD statement in either library.

targets.target: Separation of rational rank/finiteness results, p-primary valuation equalities and all-prime leading-coefficient equalities
targets.note: This is a statement-hygiene target about objects that do not exist in the libraries.

duplicates.note: BSD.8 is PS.6's declared input and owns the assembly of prime-part certificates into an exact leading term; PS.6 restates the same adapters from the motivic side.

targets.target: Certified interval/ball enclosures for period integrals and L-value expressions
targets.note: No certified enclosure framework in either library. Mathlib does have exact interval arithmetic (Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Interval/Basic.lean: arithmetic operations on NonemptyInterval with their correctness, full precision and not connected to floating point) and rigorous constant bounds such as Real.pi_gt_d20, but no ball arithmetic, no enclosure of integrals or L-values and no tactic producing them.

targets.target: Proved error bounds for the implemented families
targets.note: Mathlib has Taylor's theorem with remainder and general estimates for series, but nothing that certifies an L-value or period computation.

targets.target: Exact algebraic factors and normalization-map comparison before numerical testing
targets.note: Depends on the period objects of PS.0-PS.2, which are absent.

targets.target: Conjecture statements for period, Beilinson and higher-rank special values with dependency gates
targets.note: No conjecture is stated in either library; this part of the layer is bookkeeping rather than mathematics, but it is inseparable from the absent objects.

duplicates.note: CN.4 is PS.7's declared input and owns certified numerical evaluation with error bounds; PS.7 restates it for periods.

targets.target: Relative de Rham cohomology and the Gauss-Manin connection of an algebraic family
targets.note: grep -rn -i 'gauss-manin' over both trees returns nothing. Mathlib has connections only in the differential-geometry sense; Tau Ceti has covariant derivatives and Levi-Civita connections on vector bundles, not an algebraic Gauss-Manin connection.

targets.target: Picard-Fuchs equation by proved reduction of differential forms
targets.note: grep -rn -i 'picard-fuchs' over both trees returns nothing.

targets.target: Analytic period solutions, integral monodromy and the normalized mirror coordinate
targets.note: No mirror map, no Picard-Fuchs system and no family of varieties with its period lattice. The generic monodromy tools exist but are not applied to a family: Mathlib has monodromy of covering maps and lifting along homotopies, and Tau Ceti has local coefficient systems with their monodromy representation (TauCeti.LocalCoefficientSystem.monodromyRepresentation) and a monodromy theorem for analytic continuation.

targets.target: Good-prime integral/crystalline model and Frobenius compatibility for a quintic family
targets.note: No crystalline cohomology in either library and no Frobenius matrix on cohomology.

targets.target: K3 hypergeometric family with singular parameters, solution basis and denominator primes
targets.note: Mathlib defines the Gauss hypergeometric function 2F1 (ordinaryHypergeometricSeries, ordinaryHypergeometric, radius of convergence one) and regularized versions, but not the generalized hypergeometric functions pFq that K3 families need, nor the hypergeometric differential equation, a family of K3 surfaces, singular parameter values, solution bases or denominator primes. (Tau Ceti's hypergeometric probability distribution is unrelated.)

duplicates.note: CR.7 is PS.8's declared input and owns the crystalline coefficient interfaces and Frobenius structures PS.8 restates.
C5 proves relative Gauss-Manin compatibility for proper smooth families, which PS.8 lists as its own construction.

targets.target: Convergent multiple zeta sums with an admissibility/ordering convention
targets.note: grep -rn -i 'multiple zeta' and a name search for multipleZeta/MZV over both trees return nothing. Mathlib has riemannZeta and hurwitzZeta only.

targets.target: Iterated-integral representation on P1 minus {0,1,infinity}
targets.note: The phrase 'iterated integral' in Mathlib refers to Fubini/Tonelli for product measures and to Sobolev inequalities, not to Chen iterated integrals along a path.

targets.target: Word algebras with shuffle and stuffle products, and the regularization comparison map
targets.note: Tau Ceti has tensor words (TauCeti.TensorWords, all tensor powers of a module) with the deconcatenation coproduct and its subword calculus, but no shuffle or quasi-shuffle (stuffle) product, so no shuffle Hopf algebra; every 'shuffle' name in both trees is a sign convention or a tensor rearrangement. No tangential-base-point regularization or regularization comparison map.

targets.target: Mixed-Tate category, motivic fundamental group and coaction, and the motivic period map
targets.note: No motives at all, hence no mixed-Tate subcategory, no motivic fundamental group and no coaction.

targets.target: Low-weight shuffle/stuffle identities and Hoffman-type spanning results
targets.note: Absent; the underlying objects do not exist.

duplicates.note: MC.6 constructs tensor-automorphism groups and period torsors of neutral Tannakian categories, computes the Tate subcategory, and keeps the formal torsor statement separate from numerical period injectivity - the motivic Galois and period-map targets of PS.9 T3.

RankZeroOneBSD.summary: The arithmetic side of BSD.1 is in much better shape than the roadmap assumes: Tau Ceti has a sorry-free Mordell-Weil theorem over a number field (fg_point_of_numberField), finiteness of torsion and Nagell-Lutz, the weak Mordell-Weil theorem by explicit 2-descent, the 2-Selmer group with the rank bound it gives, the Neron-Tate canonical height with the exact parallelogram law and the Neron-Tate pairing, the regulator as a basis-independent absolute determinant (including the rank-zero convention Reg = 1 the roadmap asks BSD.9 to verify), and the quadratic twist by a separable quadratic extension with its invariants, the Galois cocycle and the point isomorphism E^L(M) = E(M) twisted by the quadratic character, which with Galois descent of fixed points gives the eigenspace inputs of BSD.1's rank identity. Mathlib supplies the reduction trichotomy over a DVR, minimal models and the local Euler factors, and assembles them into the L-function of a Weierstrass curve over a number field as a formal Euler product (WeierstrassCurve.LFunction, WeierstrassCurve.LSeries) - the Euler-product half of BSD.0. Everything analytic beyond that is missing: no modularity, no analytic continuation or functional equation of L(E,s), no root number, no conductor, no Tamagawa numbers or Kodaira types, no real period, no Sha, no Heegner points, no Gross-Zagier, no Euler systems or Kolyvagin, no Iwasawa main conjectures, no p-adic L-functions or modular symbols, and no metaplectic/half-integral-weight forms for the twist-nonvanishing theorem. So BSD.0-BSD.1 are partly built and BSD.2-BSD.9 are not built at all.

targets.target: Euler product / Dirichlet series of E over a number field
targets.note: Mathlib defines the L-function of a Weierstrass curve over any number field as the Euler product over the height-one spectrum of the ring of integers of the local Euler factors, with the four reduction cases (1 - a_p T + |p| T^2, 1 - T, 1 + T, 1) written out, and the associated LSeries. This is more general than the roadmap's E/Q. The file is sorry-free. No convergence, meromorphic continuation or uniqueness-from-a-connected-domain statement is proved about it.

targets.target: Modular entire continuation and completed functional equation of L(E,s)
targets.note: There is no modularity theorem in either library (a name search for modularity/taniyama over both trees returns only an unrelated combinatorics lemma), so the continuation cannot be transported from the modular side, and nothing proves continuation directly. Mathlib does have the completed L-function of a modular form and its functional equation, and entire continuation for cusp forms, so the target of the transport exists but the bridge does not.

targets.target: Analytic rank as the order of vanishing at s = 1, proved finite
targets.note: The general notion the layer wants - the order of vanishing of an analytic function at a point, with order 0 equivalent to a nonzero value and finiteness from non-vanishing nearby - is complete in Mathlib in full generality (also meromorphicOrderAt). What is missing is an analytic function L(E,-) to apply it to; the layer's own warning that 'an arbitrary analytic germ is not a witness' is the obstruction.

targets.target: Root-number parity relation for the analytic order
targets.note: There is no root number of an elliptic curve and no conductor of an elliptic curve in either library (name searches for conductor return only conductors of Dirichlet characters and of ring extensions). Mathlib has DirichletCharacter.rootNumber, which is the Dirichlet analogue, not the elliptic one.

targets.target: Quadratic twist with every local Euler-factor comparison and the factorization L(E/K,s) = L(E,s) L(E^K,s)
targets.note: The twist itself is built and sorry-free in Tau Ceti: over any commutative ring for quadraticTwistOf and by a separable quadratic extension for quadraticTwist, with the scaling of b2, b4, b6, c4, c6 and Delta, equality of j, the point isomorphism E^L(M) = E(M) twisted by the quadratic character, and the explicit Galois cocycle exhibiting it as an L-form. No local Euler-factor comparison between E, E^K and E/K is proved (this is a local statement about Mathlib's localPolynomial and needs no continuation), and the factorization L(E/K,s) = L(E,s) L(E^K,s) is not stated even as an identity of formal Euler products.

targets.target: Coefficient-field/rationality bridge from weight-two newforms with rational coefficients
targets.note: Tau Ceti has an extensive newform theory (TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/Newforms: multiplicity one, strong multiplicity one, Atkin-Lehner, eigenvalue fields, nebentypus descent) and Mathlib has the modular L-function, so the modular side of the bridge is substantially built; the bridge to an elliptic curve is not, because modularity is absent.

duplicates.note: R29.6 explicitly owns transferring the analytic continuation and functional equation to E after proving equality of every local factor; BSD.0 restates the same interface as its own construction.

targets.target: Mordell-Weil lattice modulo torsion, with finite generation and finite torsion
targets.note: The Mordell-Weil theorem is proved in Tau Ceti for an elliptic curve over a number field and, more generally, over the fraction field of a Dedekind domain with per-factor class-group and unit-group finiteness; the weak Mordell-Weil theorem is proved by explicit 2-descent into square classes. The quotient by torsion (PointModTorsion) and the fact that torsion lies in the kernel of the Neron-Tate pairing are both proved. All the files are sorry-free.

targets.target: Regulator and canonical height
targets.note: The canonical height is constructed by Tate's averaging with the standard 1/2 normalization (the docstring notes that the naive x-height belongs to the divisor 2(O)), the exact parallelogram law is proved, height zero is equivalent to finite order, and the regulator is the absolute determinant of the Neron-Tate Gram matrix, proved independent of the basis even across different index types. Sorry-free.

targets.target: Finite-level Selmer groups
targets.note: Only the 2-Selmer group exists, defined by square classes with trivial norm class satisfying the local condition at every finite place and at an auxiliary family of fields, together with the rank bound 2^rank * #E(K)[2] <= #S for any finite S containing the image of the descent map. Its own file records that it does not prove the Selmer group finite; the auxiliary group selmerGroupA is proved finite. There is no Selmer group at general m, no Selmer structure on a general Galois module, and no Sha at all.

targets.target: Rank identity rank E(K) = rank E(Q) + rank E^K(Q) and its lattice-index correction
targets.note: The eigenspace inputs are in Tau Ceti, sorry-free: for a separable quadratic L/K and any field M over L, quadraticTwistPointEquiv identifies E^L(M) with E(M), and transports the action of every sigma in Aut(M/K) to chi(sigma|L) times the action on E(M) - so E^L(K)-points are the sigma = -1 part of E(L) - while exists_baseChange_eq_of_map_eq descends sigma-fixed points of E(L) to E(K). Not proved: the rank identity rank E(L) = rank E(K) + rank E^L(K), the trace/restriction maps on points, or the index of E(K) + E^L(K) in E(L).

targets.target: p-primary Selmer/Sha comparison at odd p and restriction/corestriction at p = 2
targets.note: The finite-group cohomology machinery the layer needs exists: Mathlib has group cohomology with restriction and Shapiro's lemma, and Tau Ceti adds corestriction, Tate cohomology with the Herbrand quotient and continuous (profinite) cohomology with restriction/corestriction/inflation and cup products. But no Selmer or Sha group is built from it, so the comparison itself is absent.

targets.target: Component groups, minimal differentials, periods, Tamagawa factors under base change and twist; Cassels' isogeny invariance
targets.note: Mathlib has integral and minimal models over a DVR and the good/multiplicative/split-multiplicative/additive trichotomy; Tau Ceti has the invariant differential and minimal-model transfer of split multiplicative reduction. Neron models, component groups, Kodaira types, Tate's algorithm, Tamagawa numbers, the real period and Cassels' isogeny-invariance theorem are all absent from both libraries.

targets.target: Descent of Sha finiteness along a finite extension
targets.note: Sha does not exist in either library.

duplicates.note: Layer 6 owns the Mordell-Weil theorem and names the very declaration (fg_point_of_numberField) that is now in Tau Ceti; BSD.1 says it reuses it, so the overlap is intended but the target is already delivered.
Layer 7 owns Selmer structures, the Selmer group and Sha for a general Galois module; BSD.1's finite-level Selmer comparison depends on it and partly restates it.
RP.1 owns weak Mordell-Weil and descent in general, which BSD.1 uses for the twist comparison.

targets.target: Quadratic-twist nonvanishing theorem with prescribed local conditions (BFH / Friedberg-Hoffstein)
targets.note: Absent. Mathlib's only nonvanishing results for L-functions are non-vanishing of Dirichlet L-functions on the line Re s = 1 (Mathlib/NumberTheory/LSeries/Nonvanishing.lean), used for primes in arithmetic progressions; nothing concerns central values of a family of twists.

targets.target: Twists with nonzero central value in the sign + branch and nonzero first derivative in the sign - branch
targets.note: Requires the central value of L(E^K, s), which needs a continuation that does not exist.

targets.target: Metaplectic/Weil representation, Jacobi forms and genus-two half-integral-weight Eisenstein series
targets.note: Neither library has half-integral weight forms, the metaplectic double cover, the Weil representation or Jacobi forms. Mathlib has the Jacobi theta function (one and two variable) but no Jacobi form; Tau Ceti's Fourier/theta content is classical analysis.

targets.target: Unfolding, twist-series comparison, residue/positivity and local test-function selection
targets.note: No Rankin-Selberg or unfolding machinery in either library.

targets.target: Export of K with all local properties and simultaneous satisfiability for BSD.3-4
targets.note: Depends entirely on the absent nonvanishing theorem.

duplicates.note: MP.7 owns half-integral weight and metaplectic Fourier coefficients and twists, which BSD.2 imports and partly re-proves.
MP.8 owns genus-two similitudes, Jacobi forms and cover-specific Eisenstein analysis, the other half of BSD.2's imported input.

SelmerIwasawaCohomology.summary: The general continuous-cohomology substrate this roadmap imports is substantially built in Tau Ceti, but only in degrees 0, 1 and 2: an explicit complex of continuous cochains with H0, H1, H2, the comparison with Mathlib's group cohomology for discrete groups (and with Mathlib's continuousCohomology in degree 0), the colimit description of H1 over finite quotients, cup products in all bidegrees up to total degree 2 with associativity and all six projection formulas, restriction, corestriction and inflation with the degree-one inflation-restriction sequence, Shapiro in degrees 0 and 1, the long exact sequence of a discrete short exact sequence through H^2, Tate cohomology with the Herbrand quotient, and the Kummer map with its kernel, all sorry-free. Mathlib supplies the all-degree functor continuousCohomology (only H^0 computed), the Mittag-Leffler condition for cofiltered systems of types, and the topological Pontryagin dual with its functoriality. Everything specific to this roadmap is absent from both libraries: no lim^1, no Hochschild-Serre spectral sequence or five-term sequence, no local or global duality (no invariant map, no Tate local duality, no Euler-characteristic formula, no Poitou-Tate), no Selmer structure on a Galois module, no Selmer complex, no contragredient Galois dual, no Iwasawa cohomology, no completed group ring, no control theorem, no characteristic ideal and no Bloch-Kato local condition. L0 should be told that continuous cup products, corestriction, low-degree Shapiro, the discrete comparison and the Kummer injection already exist; what it genuinely still needs is the p-adic limit H^1(F, Z_p(1)) = lim_m F^x/(F^x)^{p^m}, Hilbert 90 for the separable closure (the one missing input for Kummer surjectivity), and the derived-limit apparatus.

targets.target: Compact continuous cochains and continuous cohomology
targets.note: Mathlib defines continuousCohomology in every degree as the homology of homogeneous continuous cochains for a topological group acting continuously on a topological module (so compact coefficients are covered), but computes only H^0 and lists long exact sequences and the comparison with groupCohomology as TODOs. Tau Ceti builds the explicit inhomogeneous complex in degrees <= 2, compares its H^0 with Mathlib's continuousCohomology, compares H^0, H^1 and H^2 with Mathlib's group cohomology when the group is discrete, and proves the colimit description of H^1 over the finite quotients of a profinite group. All files are sorry-free. Nothing compares cohomology with inverse-limit coefficients.

targets.target: Derived-limit comparison and the lim^1 exact sequence
targets.note: Neither library has lim^1 of an inverse system of abelian groups or the Milnor sequence; a name search for lim1/limOne/Rlim/derivedLimit over both trees finds only category-theoretic 'closed under limits' lemmas. Mathlib has AddCommGrp inverse limits but no derived functor of lim.

targets.target: Full Hochschild-Serre spectral sequence with edge maps
targets.note: Only the degree-one inflation-restriction sequence 0 -> H^1(G/N, M^N) -> H^1(G, M) -> H^1(N, M) is proved, in Mathlib (discrete) and in Tau Ceti (continuous); Tau Ceti's degree-two inflation only has res o infl = 0. There is no transgression, no five-term sequence, no Hochschild-Serre spectral sequence and no edge map; Mathlib's general spectral-sequence API is not applied to group cohomology.

targets.target: Continuous cup products, twists, duals, corestriction, Shapiro, projection formulas
targets.note: Cup products exist for every bidegree of total degree at most two (00, 01, 10, 02, 20, 11) with associativity, the projection formula in each of those bidegrees, corestriction in degrees 0, 1 and 2 with transversal-independence and cor o res = index, and Shapiro in degrees 0 and 1. Internal Hom of continuous representations is built (ContCohomology/InternalHom.lean). What is not there is a Tate twist of a Galois module, a dual in the sense the roadmap means (Pontryagin dual of a discrete module with contragredient action) or anything in degree >= 3.

targets.target: Integral Kummer comparison H^1(F, Z_p(1)) = lim_m F^x/(F^x)^{p^m}
targets.note: Tau Ceti builds the Kummer map K^x -> H^1(G_K, mu_n) for n invertible in K, computes it on cocycles, proves its kernel is (K^x)^n and hence that K^x/(K^x)^n injects into H^1(G_K, mu_n); its own docstring says surjectivity (Hilbert 90 for K^sep/K through the finite-quotient colimit) is the single missing input for the isomorphism at finite level. The p-adic limit over m, the Z_p(1) coefficient module and the comparison with a tensor-product expression for units and S-units are all absent. Mathlib's IsDedekindDomain.selmerGroup is the group K(S,n) of S-units mod n-th powers, the target of the S-restricted Kummer map.

targets.target: Which inverse-limit hypotheses hold for each tower (Mittag-Leffler bookkeeping)
targets.note: Mathlib has the Mittag-Leffler condition and eventual ranges for cofiltered systems of types (so for the underlying sets of a tower of groups), with nonempty-sections theorems, and proves that the limit of a tower of surjections surjects onto each term. Missing: lim^1 and the statement that it vanishes under Mittag-Leffler for abelian groups or modules, exactness of inverse limits of Mittag-Leffler systems, and any tower of Galois cohomology groups to which the bookkeeping could be applied.

duplicates.note: Layer 5 owns the long exact sequence, inflation-restriction and the five-term sequence with transgression - the low-degree part of the Hochschild-Serre target L0 T2 (only the three-term inflation-restriction sequence is delivered, in TauCeti ContCohomology/Inflation).
L0's own text says these general theorems are imported from ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02 and must not be reimplemented; the overlap is by design but the targets are stated in both places.
R02.2 builds the Hochschild-Serre spectral sequence with its low-degree identification and restriction/corestriction identities - L0 T2.

D7 is the declared owner of derived inverse limits with lim^1 and Mittag-Leffler conditions, full continuous Hochschild-Serre with edge maps, and the cup/cores/Shapiro normalizations - L0 T1, T2, T3 and T5.
Layer 6 owns corestriction in degrees 0-2 with transversal independence - part of L0 T3 (delivered in TauCeti ContCohomology/Corestriction).
Layer 7 owns coinduced modules and Shapiro's lemma - part of L0 T3 (delivered in degrees 0 and 1).
Layer 8 owns low-degree cup products and the projection formula - part of L0 T3 (delivered in TauCeti ContCohomology/Cup and ProjectionFormula).
Layer 9 owns profinite Hilbert 90 and the Kummer isomorphism at finite level, the input L0 T4 specializes to H^1(F, Z_p(1)).

targets.note: Neither library has the invariant map of a local field, local Tate duality or a perfect cup-product pairing H^i(K,M) x H^{2-i}(K,M') -> Q/Z. targets.note: Absent from both libraries.

targets.note: No cohomological dimension of a profinite group in either library, and no finiteness theorem for Galois cohomology of a number field. Tau Ceti proves finiteness of class groups, ray class groups and narrow class groups, which are the classical shadows of these statements, not the statements themselves.

targets.note: Depends on the Selmer local conditions of L2, which do not exist.

targets.note: Mathlib has the topological Pontryagin dual A ->t* Circle with the compact-open topology (compact for discrete A, discrete for compact A) and its contravariant functoriality PontryaginDual.map, and the character module Hom(A, Q/Z) of an abelian group. Missing: the contragredient Galois action on the dual of a discrete torsion Galois module, the involution convention, and double duality beyond finite abelian groups.

targets.note: Absent. Mathlib has mapping cones and fibres of morphisms of complexes in general homological algebra, so the categorical tool exists, but there is no Galois cochain complex over a number field to apply it to.

targets.target: Changes of local conditions, primitive/imprimitive exact sequences, lattice-change formulas
targets.note: Absent.

duplicates.note: That layer sets up Selmer structures for a general Galois module first (local-condition subgroups unramified almost everywhere, with the Selmer group inside H^1(K,M)), which is exactly L2's first target.

targets.target: Iwasawa cohomology H^i_Iw(F,T) via corestriction, identified with cohomology of the induced completed-group-ring representation
targets.note: Corestriction in degrees 0, 1 and 2 exists in Tau Ceti and would be the transition map of the inverse system. Mathlib has the closest thing to the coefficient ring: abstract measures on Z_p with values in Q_p and the Amice transform identifying them with power series, which its own docstring calls the definition of the Iwasawa algebra - but as an analytic object, not as a completed group ring Z_p[[Gamma]], and with no module theory (no characteristic ideal, no structure theorem). There is no Z_p^d-extension, no inverse limit of cohomology groups along corestriction, and hence no Iwasawa cohomology.

targets.note: Absent; none of the objects exists.

targets.target: Control theorems with explicit kernels and cokernels
targets.note: Absent from both libraries.

targets.note: No perfect complexes, no determinant functor and no characteristic ideal of a finitely generated torsion Iwasawa module in either library.

targets.note: Absent.

targets.note: The class group, its finiteness and the class number are complete in Mathlib and Tau Ceti, and Mathlib has the mod-n and p-adic cyclotomic characters that define Tate twists. But there is no Selmer group of a Tate twist and no comparison exact sequence, so the recovery statement cannot be formed.

The gamma factor exists for Dirichlet characters. No definition of criticality is stated anywhere in either library.

targets.note: No conjecture of this kind is stated in either library, and there is no p-adic L-function to state it about.

SpecialValuesBirchTate.summary: Everything K-theoretic in this roadmap is absent: neither library has K_2 or any K-group beyond K_0 (Tau Ceti has K_0 of exact categories and of finitely generated projective modules over a ring), so K_2(O_F), the tame kernel, Steinberg symbols, the localisation sequence and the whole right-hand side of Birch-Tate do not exist. Nor does the Galois module Q/Z(2), W_2(F) or w_2: Tau Ceti has only mu_n as a G_K-module, and Mathlib the p-adic cyclotomic character. On the analytic side the situation is better than the roadmap assumes only for Q: Mathlib proves zeta(-k) = (-1)^k B_{k+1}/(k+1) for every k, so zeta_Q(-1) = -1/12 is immediate, and it has the Gamma-factor apparatus (Gammaℝ, Gammaℂ, the residue at zero and the reflection identities) that B.2 wants for the gamma-pole limit, plus a general abstract functional-equation framework. For a general number field the Dedekind zeta function exists in Mathlib only as an L-series with the Dirichlet class number formula for its residue at s = 1. Tau Ceti adds its Euler product, nonvanishing on Re s > 1 and the restriction of Euler factors away from S. Neither library continues zeta_F, so there is no value at -1 and no functional equation. Missing outright: K_2 and the tame kernel, W_2 and w_2, the continuation and functional equation of zeta_F, every Iwasawa main conjecture, Kolster's implication, S-integer localisation, and all higher Lichtenbaum statements.

targets.target: W_2(F) = H^0(F, Q/Z(2)) as a cyclotomic Galois module, and w_2(F) = #W_2(F)
targets.note: The coefficients exist: Mathlib has the mod-n cyclotomic character and the Z_p^x-valued p-adic cyclotomic character (continuous on Galois groups), Tau Ceti has mu_n of the separable closure as a discrete G_K-module (KummerCoeff) with H^0 of discrete G_K-modules, and w_1(F) is NumberField.Units.torsionOrder. What is missing is Q/Z(2) as a Galois module, W_2(F) = H^0(F, Q/Z(2)) and w_2(F); the layer explicitly warns that torsionOrder is not a substitute.

targets.target: K_2(O_F), its Steinberg/tame-kernel comparison, and its finiteness
targets.note: No K_2 in either library: no Steinberg group or Steinberg symbols (the Steinberg names are Lie-theoretic, and Tau Ceti's quaternion 'Steinberg relation' is about algebras), no Milnor K-theory, no tame symbol or tame kernel and no finiteness theorem. Tau Ceti's K-theory is K_0 only (exact categories, and finitely generated projective modules over a ring).

targets.target: The analytically continued Dedekind zeta function
targets.note: Mathlib defines zeta_F as the LSeries of the ideal-counting function and proves the Dirichlet class number formula for the residue at s = 1 as a one-sided real limit; Tau Ceti proves its Euler product and its nonvanishing on Re s > 1 and computes the exact abscissa of convergence. Neither library continues zeta_F past Re s = 1, so zeta_F(-1) is not defined (Mathlib's LSeries is 0 by convention outside the region of convergence). The file's own TODO asks only to generalize the construction.

targets.target: The proposition BirchTate(F): zeta_F(-1) = (-1)^[F:Q] #K_2(O_F)/w_2(F)
targets.note: Cannot be stated: both sides are missing. Mathlib does have Module.finrank Q F for the degree and NumberField.IsTotallyReal for the hypothesis.

duplicates.note: N.4 owns the roots-of-unity-with-twists module, which is exactly B.1's W_2(F) = H^0(F, Q/Z(2)).
T.5 identifies K_2(O_F) with the tame kernel of K_2(F) via the localisation theorem and gives finite presentations - B.1 T1.

AL.1 proves continuation and the functional equation of Tate zeta integrals, which give the continued Dedekind zeta function B.1 T2 asks for (R.5 and DirichletPadicLFunctions L0 both import it from AL.1).

targets.target: zeta_F(-1) is nonzero and rational for totally real F
targets.note: zeta_F is not continued to s = -1 in either library, so neither rationality nor nonvanishing there can be stated. The analogous statement for Q is available (see B.3).

targets.target: Sign from the functional equation and positivity in the convergent half-plane
targets.note: Mathlib has a general abstract framework (WeakFEPair / IsStrongFEPair) for deriving a functional equation from a self-duality of a Mellin pair, and uses it for Dirichlet characters and modular forms; Tau Ceti proves zeta_F is nonzero for Re s > 1, which is the positivity input. ArithmeticKTheory.summary: Neither library has K_1, K_2 or higher K-theory of a ring, so K_n(O_{F,S}) for n >= 1 does not exist and almost nothing in N.2 to N.8 can be stated: there is no Quillen Q-construction or plus construction, no localisation sequence, no tame or wild kernel, and no W_j(F) = H^0(F, Q/Z(j)). What exists is K_0 and the classical low-degree shadow, sorry-free. Tau Ceti defines K_0 of the finitely generated projective modules of any ring (the split exact structure, with the Cartan map and the resolution theorem) and K_0 of split, exact, abelian and triangulated categories, but computes neither K_0(O_{F,S}) = Z + Cl nor any K_1. For S-integers it has Cl(O_S) = Cl(R)/<classes of S> with finiteness, the S-unit valuation sequence 1 -> R^x -> (O_S)^x -> Z^S and finite generation of the S-units. Mathlib has the S-integers and S-units (defined by valuations, with no presentation as a localisation), class groups and Pic, Dirichlet's unit theorem, the p-adic cyclotomic character, Bernoulli numbers with von Staudt-Clausen, and total ramification of p in Q(zeta_p). So the right-hand sides of N.1's isomorphisms and the class-group and S-unit rows of N.2 and N.3 exist in classical form. Missing are N.1's localisation presentation of O_{F,S}, N.7's topologists' Bernoulli numbering |B_2k| and every K-theoretic statement, and no layer is even partly built.

targets.target: Arithmetic carriers: number field, ring of integers, primes, O_{F,S} as a localisation, independence of presentation and compatibility with enlarging S
targets.note: The carriers exist: Mathlib defines the S-integers and S-units of the fraction field of any Dedekind domain by valuations, with O_empty = R, and Tau Ceti proves O_S is a Dedekind domain whose ideals are all extended from R and that the S-units grow with S. The layer's two theorems do not: Tau Ceti's SInteger/Basic.lean states that the S-integers are 'not in general a localization of R' and treats them only as an overring, and neither library proves that O_{F,S} is a localization of O_F for a number field (no IsLocalization instance), independence of that presentation, or monotonicity of the ring O_S in S (only the unit group, Set.unit_mono).

targets.target: K_0(O_{F,S}) is Z + Cl(O_{F,S})
targets.note: Both sides exist separately but the isomorphism does not. Tau Ceti defines K_0 of the finitely generated projective modules of any ring as the exact K_0 of finiteProjectiveModulesExactStructure R, proves that structure is the split one, and builds the Cartan map to G_0 with the resolution theorem; Mathlib identifies the class group with Pic, and Tau Ceti proves Cl(O_S) = Cl(R) modulo the classes of the primes of S, with finiteness. Nothing computes K_0 of a Dedekind domain or of O_{F,S} as Z + Cl (no rank/determinant map, no Steinitz classification).

targets.target: K_1(O_{F,S}) is O_{F,S}^x by the determinant, kept distinct from K_1(F) = F^x
targets.note: Again only the right-hand side: Mathlib identifies the S-units of K with the units of the ring of S-integers, and Tau Ceti proves that group finitely generated (Dirichlet's S-unit theorem in the finite-generation form). There is no K_1 of a ring and no determinant map out of it in either library, and no Whitehead group.

targets.note: Extension of ideals to O_S and the relative norm on class groups exist in Tau Ceti, which is the degree-zero shadow of pullback and transfer; the K-theoretic maps themselves do not exist.

Every cited declaration (163 in the audit, 182 after correction) was matched against declarations.tsv, opened at its line and compared with the target; none is private, deprecated (after replacing rank_modTorsion) or in a file with sorry, and the only index misses are Mathlib's ModularForm.Λ (verified by hand).
